## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines **sparse lexical search** (e.g. BM25) with **dense vector search**, then merges the two ranked result sets, often via reciprocal rank fusion. This approach captures both exact term matches and semantic similarity, addressing the complementary weaknesses of each method alone.

Hybrid retrieval consistently outperforms either method alone on queries that mix rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs) with natural language intent. It has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems.

## Reciprocal Rank Fusion

Reciprocal rank fusion is a technique for merging ranked result sets from multiple retrieval methods into a single ranked output. This method is commonly used as the merging strategy in hybrid retrieval pipelines.
